subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Specialty Tea Movement
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Specialty Tea Movement.

hook.text: Just like coffee's third wave, tea is experiencing a quality revolution focused on origin and craft.

buildup.text: Small-batch producers sell single-origin teas directly to consumers. Tasting notes and harvest dates matter.

discovery.text: Tea sommeliers now train formally, learning to identify hundreds of varieties by aroma, color, and flavor.

twist.text: Premium tea can be steeped multiple times—each infusion reveals different flavors from the same leaves.

climax.text: Specialty tea shops are opening in cities worldwide, offering guided tastings much like wine bars.

punchline.text: Tea has sommeliers now. The leaf is being taken seriously.

quiz.question: What can you do with premium tea leaves that you can't with tea bags?
options: Steep them multiple times, each revealing different flavors

details.summary: A specialty tea movement, parallel to third-wave coffee, is growing worldwide. It emphasizes single-origin loose-leaf teas, direct farmer relationships, and educated consumer tasting. Tea sommeliers, cupping competitions, and artisanal tea rooms are elevating tea beyond the commodity tea bag.
details.whyItMatters: The specialty tea movement shows that the quality revolution that transformed coffee is beginning to reach tea. It could reshape the industry and improve farmer incomes.
takeaways: A specialty tea movement parallels third-wave coffee
It emphasizes single-origin, loose-leaf, and direct sourcing
Tea sommeliers and cupping competitions are emerging

faq.question: How is the specialty tea movement different from traditional tea culture?
faq.answer: Traditional tea cultures in China and Japan have always valued quality, but the specialty movement brings this appreciation to Western consumers who grew up with commodity tea bags. It adds modern sourcing transparency, scientific brewing precision, and a global marketplace for rare teas.

faq.question: Where can you find specialty tea today?
faq.answer: Dedicated tea shops, online purveyors, and tea subscription services offer high-quality loose-leaf teas from specific gardens and harvests. Cities worldwide now have specialty tea rooms. The market is smaller than specialty coffee but growing rapidly as consumers discover quality tea.
